system_prompt_style.evidence_quote: we have an LLM-agnosticsystem promptstage where we teach the planning LLM the avail-able capabilities and APIs in Incalmo. We also provide the user’senvironment specificprompt to outline attack goals and environment details
system_prompt_style.note: Per-abstraction preprompt files (pre_prompt.txt/final_prompt.txt) plus environment-specific variables rendered per run.

env_context_strategy.evidence_quote: we design a queryable envi-ronment state service that maintains a structured knowledge base of the environment (akin to RAG [39]). LLMs can output high-level code that queries the service.
env_context_strategy.note: Closest values: model queries a structured state service (RAG-like retrieval) and explores via scan tasks; not lexical/embedding in the strict sense. Treat as mixed navigation+queryable-service.

context_compaction.evidence_quote: This allows the majority of accumulated knowledge to be off-loaded from the LLM, in contrast to prior systems storing all knowledge in the LLM’s context.
context_compaction.note: Environment state service maintains a structured database of Python objects offloading knowledge from context.

observation_format.evidence_quote: the agents return any results or errors, and then Sonnet 4 reacts and decides the subsequent task(s)

tool_call_format.evidence_quote: we ex-tract the Python function between the<task></task> or<query></query>tags. Then Incalmo executes the function

tool_count.evidence_quote: our abstraction for these declarative tasks follows the logical stages specified by the MITRE ATT&CK [12] and cyber kill chain [30] frame-works: scan a network, laterally move, escalate privileges, discover local information, and exfiltrate data.
tool_count.note: Five high-level declarative tasks exposed to the planner, plus a query capability. Incalmo-WHT variant exposes 19 predefined low-level tasks.

edit_primitive.evidence_quote: our abstraction for these declarative tasks follows the logical stages specified by the MITRE ATT&CK [12] and cyber kill chain [30] frame-works: scan a network, laterally move, escalate privileges, discover local information, and exfiltrate data.
edit_primitive.note: No file-edit primitive in default incalmo abstraction; a write_file low-level action exists in LowLevel actions bundle.

tool_schema_source.evidence_quote: We first create a prompt with the onboarding process outlined in Sec. 4.
tool_schema_source.note: Task/API capabilities taught via hand-written preprompt files (pre_prompt.txt, codebase.txt, final_prompt.txt).

protocol_standardization.evidence_quote: We implement a custom C&C server and use open-source malware capabilities (from the Caldera project [8])
protocol_standardization.note: Custom C&C API; no MCP/A2A client in the repo tree.

loop_primitives.evidence_quote: we explicitlydecouple planning from executionby separating Incalmo into an LLM-assisted planning layer that decideswhattasks to perform and an execution layer that decideshowto execute tasks.
loop_primitives.note: Sonnet outputs tasks, agents execute, planner reacts to results in a loop (react).

planning_granularity.evidence_quote: we reformulate it to output high-level declarative tasks inspired by the cyber kill chain frame-work
planning_granularity.note: Plan expressed as tasks emitted each step; no persisted plan object re-read across steps.

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote: The orchestrator implements the tasks with expert agents and ser-vices.
multi_agent_topology.note: Planning LLM orchestrates; default task agents are deterministic non-LLM (LLM-based agents are an opt-in extensibility case study).

delegation_mechanism.evidence_quote: We delegate the execution of these tasks to bespoke red-team agents that use reliable best practices
delegation_mechanism.note: Delegation to task agents; default agents are non-LLM deterministic executors.

human_in_loop.evidence_quote: an LLM-assisted system for autonomously red teaming multi-host networks
human_in_loop.note: Autonomous loop; no approval gate. Optional UI observes logs only.

short_term_state.evidence_quote: the environment state service maintains a structured database of Python objects that represent the environment, similar to Lore [26].

long_term_memory.evidence_quote: The database is updated as red team agents execute tasks.
long_term_memory.note: State service is within-run; no cross-run persisted memory in run loop.

state_persistence.note: Loop runs to completion/timeout; no saved-state reload path.

self_verification.evidence_quote: we create task agents that can reliably ex-ecute each of these tasks based on security domain best practices.
self_verification.note: Agents return errors to planner but harness runs no independent test/lint/judge verification by default.

retry_policy.evidence_quote: Incalmo will execute attacks until an LLM specifies a <finished>tag or reaches a time limit.
retry_policy.note: Single continuous run; no whole-task retry policy.

rollback.evidence_quote: Incalmo will execute attacks until an LLM specifies a <finished>tag or reaches a time limit.
rollback.note: No revert/rollback of actions found in run loop.

termination_condition.evidence_quote: Incalmo will execute attacks until an LLM specifies a <finished>tag or reaches a time limit.
termination_condition.note: Also terminates on a wall-clock time limit (TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 75*60), which has no matching F1 value; recorded under F3 per_run.

cost_controls.evidence_quote: We use LangChain [37] to iteratively prompt LLMs.
cost_controls.note: No token budget/routing/caching mechanism found; cost discussed only as measured outcome.

timeouts.note: Per-run 75-min limit; per-tool connect/command timeouts e.g. ConnectTimeout=3 in ssh actions.

execution_isolation.evidence_quote: Navigate to the docker directory and start the containers:
execution_isolation.note: Docker Compose attacker container; MHBench targets on OpenStack.

network_policy.note: Network egress needed to reach targets; only an IP blacklist config, empty by default.

permission_model.note: IP blocklist coded as static_allowlist per schema; empty by default (no gating).

tracing.note: Per-step JSONL action log plus logging_service and logging_schema.

replayability.note: A replay strategy exists; environment state may differ.

eval_hooks.note: MHBench environments are a separate benchmark (OpenStack/Ansible); repo has an MHBench integration mode but not the benchmark eval runner itself.

guardrails.note: IP blacklist restricts which hosts can be targeted.
